status: DRAFT - reviewer-drafted (Claude, 2026-09-27); maintainer commits; agents implement the exporter and must not change these numbers
purpose: In-house calibration coupons for the Flexible stage. Each set answers one question. Geometry for sets A, B and S is chosen to match Iacob et al. 2024 (ISO 7743 cylinder, 29 mm diameter x 12.5 mm) so results are comparable with the only tabulated FDM squish dataset.

common.bead_width_mm: job default wall line width (0.42 on his X1C profile) - record the actual value in the manifest

test.report: secant modulus at 10% and 20% nominal strain from the 4th LOADING cycle, toe extrapolated (Iacob method); keep every cycle, loading and unloading
test.optional_extra: after the 4 cycles, one further cycle to 50% nominal strain (plateau exploration) recorded separately, force limit permitting
test.platens: lubricate top and bottom surfaces (Iacob / ISO 7743)

common.weigh_every_piece: yes - mass is how printed core density is known (nominal infill % understates it), and a light piece flags missing material

sets.question: Does a TopOpt-GENERATED 1-bead gyroid squish like the slicer-infill gyroid the literature measured, at equal relative density?

arms.slicer: gyroid sparse infill at density x 100 %, wall loops 0, top/bottom shell layers 4, layer 0.2 mm

arms.export: TopOpt gyroid, beads_per_wall 1, relative density as listed, top/bottom skins 4 layers, no side skin
arms.slicer: wall generator Arachne, wall loops 1, sparse infill 0 %, top/bottom shell layers 4, layer 0.2 mm, line width = bead width

sets.notes: At 15 % the 1-bead gyroid cell is ~8.7 mm, so only ~3.4 cells span 29 mm and ~1.3 span the 10.9 mm core height - size effects are possible; record cells-across in the manifest. Proxy force at 20 % strain (varioShore-190 as stand-in): ~94 N / ~340 N / ~645 N.

sets.question: Does his printer reproduce Iacob's table? (replication)
sets.slicer: gyroid sparse infill 20 %, wall loops 0, top/bottom shell layers 4, layer 0.2 mm, 35 mm/s, part fan 70 % (Iacob settings); bed temperature 0 C (unheated) and part fan off for the first 4 layers, full from layer 6 (Iacob Table 1)
sets.pass_bar: E10 and E20 within ~15 % of Iacob's 20 % gyroid rows at each temperature (190: 2.19/1.46; 220: 0.77/0.59; 240: 0.84/0.75 MPa)

sets.question: Scale invariance / bead count: does a 2-bead gyroid squish like a 1-bead gyroid at the same relative density when the whole specimen is scaled x2?
sets.material: same TPU 95A lot as set A

arms.export: TopOpt gyroid, beads_per_wall 2, cell size = 2 x the set-A cell at the same density, top/bottom skins 8 layers (1.6 mm), no side skin

sets.compare_against: set A generated_mesh arm at 0.15 and 0.25 (every dimension of S is exactly 2x A - geometrically similar)
sets.notes: Proxy force at 20 % strain: ~375 N (15 %) and ~1360 N (25 %). Use the 200 kg load cell. Do not test 35 % at this size (> 2 kN). Layer height stays 0.2 mm (0.4 mm layers are impractical for TPU on a 0.4 mm nozzle), so bead-level geometry is NOT scaled - the same confound Justino Netto 2024 had. Interpret with that caveat.

sets.question: Sideways: does printed TPU gyroid squash the same when loaded ACROSS the print layers as ALONG them? (unlocks side faces from 'estimated')
sets.material: same TPU 95A lot as set A

arms.export: TopOpt gyroid, beads_per_wall 1, relative density as listed, solid skins on the two faces that will touch the platens (the SIDES of the printed block, 4 beads thick), no skin on the other four faces
arms.test: compress horizontally relative to print: rotate the block 90 deg so the platens press on the two skinned side faces

sets.compare_against: a vertically-loaded 29 mm cube of the same density (print 3 extra per density with skins on top/bottom instead) - same shape, only the load direction relative to the layers differs
sets.notes: Cubes rather than Iacob cylinders so the same geometry can be loaded in both directions. The 9 vertical cubes are the control; the 9 sideways cubes are the question. Evidence it may be close: gyroid geometry is cubic-symmetric, and Beloshenko 2021 found printed TPU gyroid much less direction-dependent than honeycomb.
